cards.text: Jesus has just arrived in Jerusalem, and now He walks into the temple courts. People are buying and selling right there. It's the temple courts, friend, but it's got Black Friday energy.

cards.question: Jesus walks into the temple courts and finds people buying and selling. What does He do?

answers.text: He asks them to move aside

cards.question: True or false: While Jesus drives out the buyers and sellers, He leaves the tables of the money changers standing.

cards.text: Tables FLIPPED, and the seats of the dove sellers go right over with them. Then Jesus speaks up and quotes Scripture.

cards.question: Jesus quotes Scripture to say God's house is meant to be a house of ___.
Jesus says God's house should be called a house of prayer. What does He say the people in the temple courts are making it?

cards.text: The dust settles. Then the blind and the lame come to Jesus at the temple.

cards.question: True or false: Jesus sends the blind and the lame away from the temple.

cards.text: Now the chief priests and the scribes, Israel's religious leaders, are watching. They see the wonders Jesus does, and they hear children in the temple courts shouting, "Hosanna to the Son of David!"

cards.question: The chief priests and scribes see Jesus' wonders and hear the children shouting in the temple courts. How do they feel about it?

cards.text: So they ask Jesus, "Do You hear what these children are saying?" Friend, I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, and even I could hear those children.

cards.question: True or false: Jesus tells the chief priests and scribes that yes, He hears what the children are saying.

cards.text: Then Jesus answers their question with a question of His own. Have they never read the Scripture about children and infants?

cards.question: In the Scripture Jesus quotes, God has ordained ___ from the mouths of children and infants.

cards.text: And with that, Jesus leaves them and heads out of the city for the night.

cards.question: Jesus leaves the chief priests and scribes and goes out of Jerusalem. Where does He spend the night?

cards.text: The next morning, Jesus heads back into the city, and He's hungry. By the road He spots a fig tree, so He walks up to it.

cards.question: Jesus is hungry and walks up to a fig tree by the road. What does He find on it?

cards.text: Leaves. Just leaves, like opening a cookie box and finding nothing but the paper liner. Then Jesus says to the tree, "May you never bear fruit again!"

cards.question: After Jesus tells the fig tree it will never bear fruit again, the tree withers ___.

cards.text: The disciples see the tree, and they marvel. If a batch of mine went from dough to burnt that fast, I'd be staring too.

cards.question: True or false: When the disciples see the withered fig tree, they ask Jesus why it had no figs on it.

cards.text: They want to know how the fig tree withered so quickly. Jesus answers, "Truly I tell you," and then He talks about faith.

cards.question: Jesus tells His disciples that if they have faith and do not ___, they will do what was done to the fig tree.
Jesus says faith can do even more than wither a fig tree. If His disciples tell this mountain to be lifted up, where does He say it will be thrown?

cards.text: A MOUNTAIN, into the SEA, and some days this mustache can barely lift a full mixing bowl. Then Jesus finishes with a promise about prayer.

cards.question: True or false: Jesus tells His disciples that if they believe, they will receive whatever they ask for in prayer.

findings.problem: The card says Jesus has just arrived in Jerusalem. That fact comes from before the passage (Matthew 21:10), but the card gives no reference for it and cites only Matthew 21:12.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: No card ever says that Jesus healed the blind and the lame (Matthew 21:14). Card 7 says they come to Him, and card 8 only shows that He doesn't send them away. Card 9's 'wonders' never says what He did. The baker leaves without knowing a key moment of the passage.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: In the joke, Papa Dorin says that from the junk drawer even he could hear the children in the temple courts. That puts him at a Bible event as someone who heard it. It also fails the joke logic test, because the drawer has nothing to do with that place or time, so the image doesn't click.

rule.text: Never part of a Bible event. He never says he was there, saw it or knew anyone in it. His story is only the Millers' kitchen, the junk drawer and the Dorinverse.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: 'Leaves.' / 'Just leaves, like opening a cookie box…' / 'Then Jesus says to the tree…'. It isn't the opening card.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card retells the disciples' question from Matthew 21:20 ('how the fig tree withered so quickly') but cites only Matthew 21:21. It should cite Matthew 21:20-21.

rule.text: Cite exactly what the card uses. Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The card asks the baker to guess the wording in Jesus' line, 'thrown into the sea'. Nothing told so far makes 'sea' more reasonable than 'valley' or 'desert', so the answer comes down to luck or memorized wording.

rule.text: Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.
